minutes.headline: Board sets FY27 overlay reserve target and keeps new-growth estimate flat, amid ongoing tax-billing system problems
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors reviewed monthly tax billing status, FY2026 warrants, and ongoing "bridge" errors between the CAMA and financial systems, then set FY27 planning figures: new growth estimate and an overlay reserve target. The board also reviewed a draft assessor website redesign, discussed a lack of statutory criteria for the discretionary Clause 18 hardship exemption, reviewed the assessor's office draft FY27 budget and a new project auditing 358 land condition adjustments, then entered executive session to review abatement/exemption applications.

votes.motion: Maintain $400,000 as the projected new growth estimate for FY27
Set the FY27 overlay reserve target at $260,000
Adjourn the open meeting and enter executive session under Purpose 7, not to return to open session, to review abatement/exemption applications

budget_items.what_was_said: The tax rate for fiscal 2026 was certified by the Bureau of Accounts on December 4, 2025, and is a few cents higher than last year.
The assessing assistant processed the warrant and commitment for real estate billing; a figure initially heard as billions was corrected on the record to millions.
A separate warrant amount was given for personal property billing, rendered inconsistently in the captions.
The board compared several recent years' actual new-growth figures and chose to keep the FY27 estimate the same as the prior two years, citing no known new large projects.
The principal assessor walked through building the FY27 overlay figure from this year's budgeted amount, adding an estimate for senior means-tested exemptions and an inflation adjustment.

budget_items.topic: FY2023 overlay transfer for lake-area abatements
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff recalled that a surge of abatements tied to a valuation dispute for lake-area properties required an emergency transfer into the overlay account that year.
The board reviewed last year's senior means-tested exemption applicants and total granted, and set a higher estimated applicant count for FY27 planning.

budget_items.topic: Total exemptions and abatements granted, recent years
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff and the board compared exemption totals, state reimbursement amounts, and prior-year abatement spending drawn from the overlay account.
The principal assessor presented a draft FY27 department budget showing a percentage increase over FY26, driven mainly by contracted services and mileage.
The line for outside measure-and-list contracting decreased because the office hired an in-house data collector, though salaries rose to offset it.
The mileage budget line was estimated higher due to additional inspections from ongoing projects and a plan to bring cyclical inspections in-house.
A quarterly MLS subscription fee is used to confirm sales data for assessments.
Staff identified undocumented land condition adjustments on record cards, split between residential and commercial parcels, that must be reviewed under a state directive.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors set the FY27 overlay reserve target, the account that funds abatements and exemptions, in a unanimous vote.
The board voted to keep the FY27 new-growth estimate flat with the prior two years, citing no known large new projects.
Staff described ongoing "bridge" errors between the CAMA valuation system and the town's financial system affecting tax billing.
The board reviewed a draft FY27 assessors' office budget showing an increase driven by contracted services and mileage.
The board decided to leave the discretionary Clause 18 hardship exemption without written numeric criteria, continuing case-by-case review.

why_it_matters: The overlay reserve and new-growth estimate are planning inputs that feed directly into how the FY27 tax rate and levy capacity get set.
Residents seeking a hardship abatement under Clause 18 will continue to have their applications judged individually rather than against a published standard.
Ongoing errors between the town's valuation and financial systems touch the accuracy of tax bills already mailed.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the votes actually captured (the $260,000 overlay target, the $400,000 growth-estimate motion, land condition factors, and most senior exemption figures), and several of our garbled digit strings resolve cleanly against the official text as caption errors. The most important gap is structural, not textual: the official minutes cover a full Executive Session — 5 real estate exemptions voted and approved, 3 FY26 abatements deferred — plus routine office-status items (abutters requests, excise abatements, tax-bill mailing, a DOR staffing posting) that our recording-based minutes never touch at all, while several of our decision items (Data Scout staging, who drafts the FY25 annual report, attendee roles) differ substantively enough from the official account to need checking against the recording.
